title: contextual-telemetry-diff-annotator-and-auto-hypothesis-notes
author: Aisha Raman
description: Motivation: On-call responders frequently need compact diffs of telemetry around incidents with human-friendly annotations that link to likely root-cause signals. This PR adds a lightweight 'telemetry diff annotator' that ingests two telemetry rollups (pre/post window) and produces a compact prioritized list of signal deltas with context, suggested hypotheses, and quick mitigation hints. Key goals: reduce time-to-first-hypothesis for oncall, make noisy deltas easier to triage, and provide a reproducible CLI for runbook authors. Implementation summary: added an annotator core implementing percentile-aware delta scoring, contextual enrichment from service metadata tags, and a short natural-language hypothesis generator that uses templated rules (no LLMs). The annotator produces a JSONL stream and a human-friendly CLI table. Also added a 'guided-mitigation' hinter that combines severity, delta magnitude, and historical action templates to suggest 1-3 safe next steps. Checklist: [x] design docs: docs/oncall/annotator.md [x] core annotator library [x] CLI for diff-annotate [x] unit tests + fixtures [x] docs and usage examples [x] manual QA against two incident traces Implementation notes and usage: The primary entrypoint is slo_toolkit.telemetry.annotator.Annotator which exposes annotate(pre_rollup, post_rollup, metadata) and returns a list of annotated signals with fields: signal, delta_percentile, baseline, current, score, hypothesis, mitigation_hints. The CLI is slo-toolkit diff-annotate: it accepts two rollup files and an optional --service-tag. Example output snippet (table): | signal | delta_pct | score | hint | hypothesis |. Example JSON line: {"signal":"http.latency.p95","baseline":120,"current":360,"delta_percentile":0.98,"score":9.2,"hypothesis":"backend CPU saturation on shard A","mitigation_hints":["scale-pool:redis-read","restart:worker-group-b (safe)"]}. No breaking changes to public APIs. Backwards compatibility: helper utilities are additive and default-on behind feature flag SLO_TOOLKIT_DIFF_ANNOTATOR=false. Links: design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-9082/telemetry-diff-annotator, runbook example: https://docs.internal/redwood/oncall/annotator, CLI usage: https://redwood.dev/slo-toolkit/cli/diff-annotate. Testing performed: unit tests for scoring math, fixture-driven end-to-end run against two historical incidents, and manual validation with oncall. Performance note: annotator computes deltas in O(n) over signals with small constant factors; typical run for 10k signals finishes in ~120ms on a dev machine.
